To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Flax fiber reinforced composites have shown a reduction in the tensile and flexual properties after water immersion at both temperatures.
the tensile and flexual properties of the natural fiber reinforced composites decreased with increase in moisture uptake.

1) the water absorption rate increases with increasing fiber volume fraction; 2) the tensile and flexual strengths of flax fiber/epoxy composites decrease with increasing fiber content and with increasing water absorption; 3) the tensile properties are more affected by water absorption than the flexural properties; and 4) the degradation in the mechanical properties of composites is significant at 90 °C.

water absorption in flax fiber reinforced composite materials is a significant problem and needs to be taken into consideration in the design of composite materials.
the water absorption of flax fiber epoxy composite is dependent on the fiber content.
the water uptake of flax fiber is significantly higher than glass fiber.

the mechanical properties of the flax fiber reinforced composites are highly dependent on the water uptake.
the mechanical properties of the flax fiber epoxy composites are significantly affected by the moisture absorption.
the tensile properties of the composites decrease as the water absorption rate increases.
